title:
On-call and Incident Response Playbook
Comprehensive Guide
author: Evan Lin
body:
SUMMARY:
This playbook is Redwood Inference's canonical guide for on-call operations and incident response. It consolidates the incident lifecycle (detection, classification, mitigation, communications, and post-incident review), runbook templates for common failure modes, postmortem expectations, rotation policies, game day guidance, and standard status page / customer communication templates.

SCOPE:
- Applies to all production-facing services: inference-api, model-router, kv-cache, batch-compiler, and control-plane services.
- Intended audience: on-call engineers, SREs, service owners, incident commanders, support, and customer-facing teams.

KEY OBJECTIVES:
- Reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to restore (MTTR).
- Keep customers informed with clear, timely communication.
- Capture root causes and actionable remediation in postmortems to prevent recurrence.

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
- Primary on-call (Primary): First responder for alerts and first triage.
- Secondary on-call (Secondary): Escalation target for complex incidents or prolonged toil; provides backup.
- Incident Commander (IC): Owns triage, run of incident call, decisions on mitigations and customer comms for Sev1/Sev2. Typically the Senior engineer or SRE for the service.
- Communications Lead: Coordinates status page, customer emails, and internal incident summaries.
- Postmortem Lead: Compiles timeline, root cause analysis, and action items.
- Engineering Manager / Service Owner: Approves rollout/rollback action and prioritizes fixes.

SEVERITY DEFINITIONS AND SLOS:
1) Sev1 (SEV1 - Critical): Service is down or >50% traffic impacted for >5 minutes, data loss, or security incident.
   - Target response: Acknowledge in < 1 minute.
   - Target restore: Mitigate within 60 minutes if possible; otherwise hourly updates.
2) Sev2 (SEV2 - Major): Significant degradation (20-50% impact), user-facing errors affecting functionality.
   - Target response: Acknowledge in < 5 minutes.
   - Target restore: Mitigate within 4 hours.
3) Sev3 (SEV3 - Minor): Degraded non-critical functionality, increased error rate but limited customer impact.
   - Target response: Acknowledge in < 1 business hour.
   - Target restore: Mitigate within 3 business days or scheduled fix.

ALERT TRIGGERS (examples):
- inference-api 5xx rate > 5% over 3m and absolute requests impacted > 100/min -> Sev2 threshold.
- model-router latency P99 > 1.2s for 5m -> Sev2.
- kv-cache miss rate spike > 30% coupled with increased token cost -> Sev2.
- control-plane DB connectivity loss -> Sev1.

ESCALATION PATH (quick reference):
1) Primary on-call acknowledges alert in PagerDuty and joins #oncall Slack channel.
2) If not resolved within 15 minutes or if complexity > 15m, page Secondary.
3) If incident meets Sev1 criteria or cross-team scope, IC is nominated (Primary or Senior SRE).
4) IC calls an incident bridge (Zoom link pinned in #oncall) and assigns roles (scribe, comms, mitigation owner).

INCIDENT LIFECYCLE PROCEDURE (numbered):
1) Detection & Acknowledgement
   - Acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty. Post initial summary to #oncall with service, symptoms, and immediate impact.
2) Triage & Classification
   - Identify affected service(s), scope, and severity using metrics and logs (Grafana, Loki).
   - If Sev1/Sev2, start an incident bridge and notify IC.
3) Containment & Mitigation
   - Follow service-specific runbook (see RUNBOOK TEMPLATES). Prioritize customer-facing mitigations (traffic reroute, scaling, rollback).
4) Communications
   - Communications Lead publishes an initial status page entry and an internal incident summary. Use templates below.
   - Provide updates every 30m for Sev1, hourly for prolonged Sev2, and at major milestones for others.
5) Recovery & Verification
   - Validate service health against SLOs and test critical flows. Run canary traffic for 30m if rollback/rollforward performed.
6) Incident Closure
   - IC confirms stability, posts final status page update, and closes incident when metrics stable for 60m (Sev1) or as appropriate.
7) Postmortem
   - Postmortem Lead creates a postmortem within 72 hours. Postmortem must include timeline, root cause, corrective actions, owners, and ETA.

RUNBOOK TEMPLATES (copyable):
- Runbook: inference-api high 5xx rate
  1) Check Grafana dashboard: inference-api > 5xx-rate, latency P50/P95/P99.
  2) Run quick log query: 
     - kubectl -n prod logs -l app=inference-api --since=10m | head -n 200
  3) Check model-router health and kv-cache metrics.
  4) If recent deploy in last 30 minutes, roll back to previous release:
     - tctl deploy rollback inference-api --to-version=stable
  5) If CPU/memory saturation detected, scale replicas:
     - kubectl -n prod scale deployment/inference-api --replicas=6
  6) If root cause is third-party model provider or upstream storage, open escalation with partner and apply circuit-breaker to affected model routes.
  7) Add mitigation note to incident timeline and update status page.

- Runbook: model-router increased latency (P99)
  1) Check GPU allocation and load: gcloud compute instances list (or internal fleet UI).
  2) Verify KV cache hit-rate: /internal/metrics/kv-cache/hitrate.
  3) If one region overloaded, route traffic to fallback region per routing policy:
     - python tools/route_traffic.py --from=us-west1 --to=us-east1 --policy=fallback
  4) If model version causing latency, route traffic to quantized variant:
     - curl -X POST https://control-plane/route -d '{"model":"redwood-llama-v2-q4"}'

- Runbook: control-plane DB connectivity loss
  1) Check DB cluster status and replicas. 2) Failover to read-replica if primary unreachable. 3) Pause non-essential writes and notify product owners.

POSTMORTEM TEMPLATE (required fields):
- Title (service + summary)
- Incident ID (PD-YYYYMMDD-N)
- Timeline (minute-by-minute until stabilized)
- Impact statement (customers, SLOs, revenue, support tickets)
- Root cause analysis (5 Whys / Fishbone)
- Corrective actions (short-term and long-term) with owners and due dates
- Rollout / deployment lessons and post-deployment checks to add to CI/CD
- Prevention plan and acceptance criteria
- Links to logs, dashboards, and PRs

ON-CALL ROTATIONS AND SCHEDULING:
- Rotation model: 1-week primary rotations with 1-week secondary buffer.
- Typical schedule: Primary Monday 08:00 local -> next Monday 08:00.
- Handoff: incoming Primary does a 15-minute handoff with outgoing Primary in #oncall with summary of ongoing incidents, degradations, and planned maintenance.
- Timezone coverage: Team aims to provide 24/7 coverage using regional on-call pools (US, EU, APAC) and cross-region backup.
- Vacation/Supplements: Engineers must declare out-of-office in the on-call rota at least 2 weeks in advance. Use swap tool (oncall-swap) for emergency handover.

GAME DAYS (exercises) GUIDELINES:
- Frequency: Quarterly for each major service; at least two company-wide tabletop exercises per year.
- Objectives: Validate runbooks, test escalation paths, exercise comms templates, and measure MTTA/MTTR.
- Scenarios: Model-serving outage, data corruption, large-scale traffic surge, and security compromise.
- After-action: Game day lead produces a short report with metrics and action items; owners assigned and tracked until complete.

STATUS PAGE & CUSTOMER COMMUNICATION TEMPLATES:
- Status Page Entry (initial):
  Title: Degraded performance in inference API (Region: us-west1)
  Impact: Customers in us-west1 may experience increased latency and 5xx errors for text generation requests.
  Current status: Investigating.
  Next update: in 30 minutes or when new information is available.

- Customer Email (acknowledgement):
  Subject: Incident affecting Redwood Inference: text generation latency in us-west1
  Body: Hello, we are investigating increased latency and errors affecting text generation in region us-west1. Our engineering team is working to identify the cause and implement mitigations. We will provide updates every 30 minutes. If you are experiencing production-impacting errors, please reply to this email with your account id and request examples.

- Status Page Update (mitigation):
  Current status: Mitigation in progress. Traffic is being routed to fallback region and the rollback is in progress. Errors have decreased by ~70% but some customers may see intermittent failures.
  Next update: in 30 minutes.

- Final Resolution (closure):
  Summary: The incident was caused by a faulty model rollout that increased request latency and error rates. We rolled back to the previous stable model and restored normal traffic routing.
  Impact: Affected customers in us-west1 may have seen elevated errors between 09:12-10:48 UTC. No data loss detected.
  Actions taken: Rollback, routing to fallback region, postmortem in progress.

COMMUNICATIONS BEST PRACTICES:
- Be timely, transparent, and avoid speculation. State known facts, impact, and next steps.
- Coordinate with legal and customer success for security incidents or large-enterprise impacts.
- Use the Communications Lead to manage external messaging and internal exec updates.

APPENDIX: CONTACTS, TOOLS, AND CHECKLISTS
- Tools: PagerDuty (alerts), Slack (#oncall, #incidents), Zoom (incident bridge), Grafana, Loki, BigQuery (log archive), internal control-plane UI.
- Escalation contacts (example):
  - On-call PagerDuty: see rota (link to rota).
  - SRE Lead: Jonah Reyes (pager: +1-555-0102).
  - Platform Owner: Asha Kapoor (slack: asha).

- Pre-incident checklist (for incoming Primary):
  1) Confirm PagerDuty notification settings and mobile connectivity.
  2) Verify access to production dashboards and runbook links.
  3) Ensure handover notes posted in #oncall.

CHANGE LOG:
- 2026-02-15: Created by Evan Lin.
- 2026-03-01: Reviewed and published; updated runbooks for inference-api and added game day cadence.

RELATED DOCUMENTS:
- SLO and error budget policy: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets
- CI/CD rollback policy: /confluence/eng-platform/ci-cd-and-deployments
- Security incident response: /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security

If you are reading this as an on-call engineer: bookmark this page, ensure PagerDuty is enabled, and join the weekly on-call sync for any open action items.
